headline: OpenAI used its own LLMs to design its Jalapeño chip, drastically shortening design time
summary: OpenAI's Jalapeño chip, designed with the help of its own LLMs, saw its development time drastically reduced. This innovative approach suggests future chip designs could be even faster.
details: OpenAI's Jalapeño chip was designed using its own LLMs, significantly cutting down development time. This innovative method promises even faster chip design cycles in the future.
The Jalapeño chip itself features a compute die, six stacks of HBM4, and an I/O chiplet. This configuration indicates a high-performance design tailored for demanding AI workloads.

This development highlights the growing capability of AI in complex engineering tasks, moving beyond software to influence hardware creation directly. It showcases a new frontier in autonomous design and manufacturing.

headline_marked: [[Anthropic confirms operating a wet biology lab]] in the Bay Area, using AI for physical experiments
headline: Anthropic confirms operating a wet biology lab in the Bay Area, using AI for physical experiments
summary: The AI research firm, known for its safety warnings, is now conducting physical experiments with its AI models, raising questions about the balance between innovation and potential risks.
details: AI research firm Anthropic has confirmed it is operating a wet biology lab in the Bay Area. The lab allows the company to use its AI models to conduct physical experiments, moving beyond purely digital simulations.

This move aligns with the broader AI industry's vision, where leaders like Dario Amodei suggest AI could cure major diseases within 5-10 years. Real-world lab work is considered essential to test these AI-driven theories.

Eric Kauderer-Abrams, Anthropic's head of life sciences, stated that the lab functions like typical biotech facilities, engaging in internal research and collaborating with external partners. This follows Anthropic's acquisition of stealth AI biotech Coefficient Bio in April.

Anthropic clarified that the lab's primary focus is fundamental biology, not drug discovery, to avoid competing with its numerous pharmaceutical customers and partners. The company has previously faced backlash for products perceived to rival customer offerings.

To support the pharma industry, Anthropic also launched a Life Sciences Verification Program, granting vetted bio researchers access to its advanced models. It has published reports on accelerating protein design and uplifting bimolecular modeling.

However, this development comes amid heightened internal and external warnings about AI's existential risks. A former Anthropic researcher and the company's own alignment lead have voiced concerns about AI's potential to exterminate humanity.

CEO Dario Amodei has called for industry self-regulation and repeatedly highlighted bioterrorism as one of AI's biggest risks. The juxtaposition of these warnings with a biology lab has drawn attention and critical commentary from tech figures.
